notes: Created from the working 1.15 source after memory-profile refactor v1 and signed-update/rollback v2.
The copied factory database/release metadata remains stamped 1.15 until 1.16 release preparation is explicitly run.
This tree is not redistribution-ready merely because the version transition succeeded.

Memory diagnostics v3.1 adds type-aware recipe/salvage recovery scoring, empty-candidate downgrading, winner/runner-up margins, and diagnostic-only nearest masked code landmarks when an exact root signature has zero hits.

Memory session recovery v4 can temporarily recover Character-local recipe/salvage header drift only after the signed profile root chain has passed semantic validation. It requires a unique strong namespace-compatible winner across three samples, is not persisted, and is disabled during signed profile candidate validation.

Memory root recovery v5 can temporarily recover small fixed-byte drift in identity, selected-server, and roster code signatures. It requires a unique best nearest masked landmark, proves identity/roster/Entity name agreement and Character vitals across three samples, is never persisted, and is disabled during signed profile candidate validation.

Integrated recovery self-test v5.1 exercises the actual GameInventoryReader.read path with simultaneous in-memory drift of all three root signatures and both recipe/salvage Character header groups. It proves exact root and exact inventory failure first, then requires v5 root recovery followed by v4 inventory recovery, with no persistent memory-definition changes.

Stale-empty inventory guard v5.2 closes a recovery gap discovered by the integrated v5.1 test: a moved recipe/salvage collection can leave the old header all-zero, which is structurally indistinguishable from a legitimate empty inventory. Zero totals now trigger only a bounded type-aware proof scan; genuine empty inventories remain valid, while a strong moved collection enters the existing three-sample v4 recovery gate.

Structural-drift diagnostics v6 add bounded observational scans for roster record name/Entity fields, Entity name/Character fields, a common Character vitals shift, and recipe/salvage entry Definition/quantity/internal-name/recipe-level fields. These candidates are diagnostic only, never auto-adopted, and never persisted.

Structural recovery qualification harness v6.1 adds no production recovery behavior. It runs baseline, independent structural-family drift, combined structural drift, root+structural, inventory+structural, and root+inventory+structural scenarios across three fresh samples, recording known-good candidate retention, ranking, runner-up margins, clear-winner status, and cross-sample stability.

Structural diagnostics v6.2 anchor recipe/salvage entry-layout inspection through the existing type-aware inventory-header scan. A diagnostic entry anchor now requires a clear strong namespace/quantity-valid winner rather than the nearest merely-plausible raw header.

Memory validation tools now write full JSON result artifacts to %LOCALAPPDATA%\FieldCrafter\diagnostics and print only the result path. This convention is used by the v5.2 integrated test, v6 structural test, v6.1 qualification harness, and v6.2 qualification harness.

Structural diagnostics v6.3 remove the circular dependency between inventory-header validation and entry-layout validation. If the v4/v5.2 type-aware header scan cannot prove a header because Entry/Definition offsets drifted, diagnostics jointly score bounded hypotheses containing the Character header, Entry quantity, Entry Definition pointer, Definition internal-name pointer, and recipe level. Complete semantic hypotheses are diagnostic/qualification-only and are never auto-adopted or persisted.

Structural session recovery v7 promotes the qualified v6.3 deeper-layout evidence into a conservative, non-persistent production fallback. It recovers roster/Entity/Character/vitals/inventory-entry layout only as one coherent three-sample semantic structure, retries the normal production inventory reader, and never changes signed memory definitions. Signed candidate-profile validation explicitly disables v4, v5, and v7 recovery.

Structural recovery v7.1 calibrates the qualified pointer margins by field: roster->Entity remains >=5 while Entity->Character uses >=4, matching the live integrated v7 observation. Exact trusted-name agreement, clear-winner status, three-sample exact-layout stability, >=5 entry-pair/joint-hypothesis margins, and the full production retry remain unchanged. The v7.1 live harness also fixes the prior entry_layout_only scenario so it moves only Entry/Definition fields rather than the entire deeper object graph.
